rules.rule: Archive-entry to ROM matching, on top of the src/*.rs rule. Check: any matcher pairing an archive entry with a ROM by name alone tells same-name candidates apart by CRC before the pairing drives a destructive action (trash, prune, rewrite); falling back to an arbitrary candidate when none matches by CRC is a finding; a change widening or narrowing what an entry matches names, in the matcher's doc comment, the consumers that inherit it (check-roms, export-roms, rebuild-roms pruning). Also apply the src/*.rs rule: README.md and CHANGELOG.md cover user-visible changes under the version in Cargo.toml.

Wii U, export and purge paths, which delete files and folders. Check: A command that writes into a user-chosen directory must not recursively delete a directory it did not create in this run. Replace-directory semantics must match the bail-or-skip hygiene of copy_file(..., false), and any deletion computed from per-file metadata must fail closed: a parse error in a referencing file keeps the candidates rather than releasing them for deletion. Also apply the src/*.rs rule: oxyRomon subcommand module. Check: every CLI flag, default value, and behaviour the diff introduces or changes is documented in the matching README.md section, including the flag's interaction with existing options; a change to how roms, DATs or CHDs are matched, renamed or deduplicated contradicts the workflow section or the FAQ, so check those too; CHANGELOG.md gets an entry under the version heading that matches Cargo.toml's version for anything user-visible — a new flag, a new default behaviour, a directory the tool now deletes; do not report internal refactors with no user-visible effect. Also check: one boundary label per `?`-chain, since the same `with_context` label applied twice to one chain renders twice; per-system DAT download outcomes (imported, up to date, failed) come from the one collector in download_dats.rs, and a GraphQL mutation in mutation.rs that loops over systems itself instead is a finding.

wux-rs, which writes NUS folders into a caller's directory. Check: A command that writes into a user-chosen directory must not recursively delete a directory it did not create in this run. Replace-directory semantics must match the bail-or-skip hygiene of copy_file(..., false), and any deletion computed from per-file metadata must fail closed: a parse error in a referencing file keeps the candidates rather than releasing them for deletion.

OxyRomon subcommand module. Check: every CLI flag, default value, and behaviour the diff introduces or changes is documented in the matching README.md section, including the flag's interaction with existing options; a change to how roms, DATs or CHDs are matched, renamed or deduplicated contradicts the workflow section or the FAQ, so check those too; CHANGELOG.md gets an entry under the version heading that matches Cargo.toml's version for anything user-visible — a new flag, a new default behaviour, a directory the tool now deletes; do not report internal refactors with no user-visible effect. Also check: one boundary label per `?`-chain, since the same `with_context` label applied twice to one chain renders twice; per-system DAT download outcomes (imported, up to date, failed) come from the one collector in download_dats.rs, and a GraphQL mutation in mutation.rs that loops over systems itself instead is a finding.

chd-rs codec glue, on top of the Rust rule. Check: a constant assumed length or shape of another component's output that the code strips, skips or seeks past (a container header, a magic, a fixed prefix) is validated with a runtime check returning an error, not a debug_assert: release builds skip the assert and silently misalign every record after it.

MCP tool surface reviewed as the interface the model actually reads. Check: every value list in a tool description or parameter doc comment matches exactly what the validation code and the synthesized clap parser accept, including case; every parameter doc comment states the semantics the handler applies to the value (for example a list value replacing the whole list), not only its type; any boolean whose true value triggers an irreversible action defaults so that omitting it reaches the refusal path; a tool reporting per-system outcomes (imported, up to date, failed) maps the shared collector's result from download_dats.rs rather than looping over systems itself; one boundary label per `?`-chain, since the same `with_context` label applied twice to one chain renders twice.

OxyRomon README reviewed as prose against the code it documents. Check: every flag, default, path, command example and supported-format claim still matches the clap definition and the module that implements it, including code added in this diff; counts and lists it states (supported systems, formats, flags) match what the code accepts; two sections of the document do not contradict each other; the diff does not leave a section describing behaviour the diff removed.

Shell scripts reviewed against Cargo.toml. Check: every cargo feature, package name and binary the script names still exists after the diff; a diff that removes a feature updates every script, workflow and Dockerfile that names it.

Generated wiki under openwiki/. Check: every repo:// resource path referenced in .claims exists at head, and every claim about external tools, spawned processes or build files still matches the module that implements it; a diff that deletes a source module or drops the last external tool must trigger a wiki refresh. A claim that a build dependency is gone is checked against Cargo.lock at head too, not only the Dockerfile or manifests: a crate can stay in the graph after the binary it wraps is no longer invoked.

Test DAT fixture. Check: the header <name> is the file name without its date and extension, as in the other fixtures (`Test System (20200721) (MAME).dat` has `<name>Test System (MAME)</name>`), so imported system names stay predictable; every rom's size and hashes match the fixture file the tests feed it, and a rom with a `merge` attribute matches its parent's by CRC.
